Wald confidence intervals for Hawkes model parameters

Source: R/hawkes_fit.R
confint.hawkes_fit.Rd

Computes Wald confidence intervals for Hawkes model parameters using the observed information (negative Hessian) as a covariance estimate.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'hawkes_fit'
confint(object, parm = NULL, level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

object

A hawkes_fit object.

parm

Optional parameter subset (currently unused).

level

Confidence level for the interval. Default is 0.95.

...

Additional arguments passed to other methods.

Value

A tibble with point estimates and lower/upper bounds using confint() style column names.

Details

Fixed parameters, if any, are excluded when computing intervals.

See also

hessian_est(), confint()

Examples

set.seed(123)
spatial_region <- create_rectangular_sf(0, 10, 0, 10)

params <- list(
  background_rate = list(intercept = -4),
  triggering_rate = 0.75,
  spatial = list(mean = 0, sd = 0.75),
  temporal = list(rate = 2)
)
hawkes <- rHawkes(params, time_window = c(0, 50), spatial_region = spatial_region)
est <- hawkes_mle(hawkes, inits = params)
confint(est)
#> Asymptotic confidence inervals are known to undercover. Consider bootstrap methods.
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   Variable                  Estimate std_error  Lower  Upper
#>   <chr>                        <dbl>     <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 background_rate.intercept   -3.65     0.114  -3.87  -3.43 
#> 2 triggering_rate              0.501    0.0580  0.387  0.615
#> 3 spatial.mean                 0        0.0670 -0.131  0.131
#> 4 spatial.sd                   0.688    0.0525  0.585  0.791
#> 5 temporal.rate                2.38     0.360   1.67   3.08 


params <- list(
  background_rate = list(intercept = -4.5, z = 1),
  triggering_rate = 0.5,
  spatial = list(mean = 0, sd = 0.75),
  temporal = list(rate = 2),
  fixed = list(spatial = "mean")
)
data("example_background_covariates")
hawkes <- rHawkes(
  params,
  c(0, 50),
  example_background_covariates,
  covariate_columns = "z",
  spatial_burnin = 1
)
est <- hawkes_mle(hawkes, inits = params)
confint(est)
#> Asymptotic confidence inervals are known to undercover. Consider bootstrap methods.
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   Variable                  Estimate std_error  Lower  Upper
#>   <chr>                        <dbl>     <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 background_rate.intercept   -4.27     0.177  -4.61  -3.92 
#> 2 background_rate.z            0.952    0.0567  0.841  1.06 
#> 3 triggering_rate              0.502    0.0598  0.385  0.619
#> 4 spatial.sd                   0.784    0.0730  0.641  0.927
#> 5 temporal.rate                2.04     0.385   1.28   2.79
